**Alan Michael Garber** (born 1955) is an American physician, health economist, and academic administrator. He is the Provost of Harvard University.




## Early life and education[edit]


Garber was born in 1955.[1] He graduated from Harvard College in 1976 with an AB in economics[1] and stayed at Harvard to earn an AM and a PhD in economics.[1] While pursuing his PhD, he enrolled simultaneously at Stanford University, where he received an MD degree in 1983.[2]



## Career[edit]


Garber succeeded Steven Hyman as the provost of Harvard University on September 1, 2011.[2]
